**Triage: routing only — `domain:skills`. ⛔ No grading, no priority, no `pm:*` state, and that is deliberate.**

SKILL.md: **skills 车道 finding 由该席自分诊,全仓轮跳过.** ⇒ the whole-repo triage round routes a skills-lane finding and stops; the `domain:skills` seat grades its own. `domain:*` is triage's sole product, so this round supplies that and nothing else — the `finding` label stays on, awaiting that seat's first grading.

### Landing surface

The PM state model itself (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`) — governed.

### ⭐ Corroborated independently by this round, ⛔ not merely acknowledged

This card measures `label:finding` at **2% precision** as the ungraded index (385 of 395 open cards carrying it are already graded). **This round measured the same class from the other end and got the same answer**, on a fresh pull at 2026-09-10:

- objectui: **116** open cards carry `finding` **alongside a pm state** (i.e. already graded) — against **0** genuinely ungraded once this round's sweep finished.
- objectstack: **87** open cards in the same condition.

⇒ two independent measurements, two days apart, on both boards. The state model says 定级即离标 and practice does not do it, so the label answers a question it cannot answer.

⚠️ This round removed the stale `finding` only from cards it was itself re-grading (roughly 20), ⛔ deliberately not sweeping the rest: a 200-card label cleanup is a script's job, not a triage round's, and doing it by hand would have been unauditable. ⇒ **that backlog is this card's, and it is the reason it should not sit ungraded.**

Reading chosen (seat reading; the standing text decides): the card's reading 1 — the rule as written stands, and the triage seat already strips on grading since R+166, so what remains is (a) the one-time sweep and (b) a report-only H row 「`finding` + any `pm:*` state or `priority:*`」 so recurrence is visible on the patrol. Reading 2 (`finding` as provenance) would change the state model's meaning — the maintainer's call, ⛔ not this seat's, and ⛔ not filed as a decision because the standing text already answers and no seat has asked for the other meaning; if the maintainer wants provenance, that is one word on a card of their own. p3: the triage seat already routes around the index (it filters by pm state), so the cost is precision, not a lost card. The sweep is where the care goes: a `scripts/pm/` script, `--dry-run` by default, `--repo` for both boards, bounded batches with the rate reading before and after, stop on the first `403`/`429`, a resume cursor — a 200-write burst on the shared identity is #17374's incident class, ⛔ never a loop. Run once by the seat that owns the board it sweeps. Two deliverables: D1 = the sweep script (free file, not governed); D2 = the H row, serial on the `check-half-states.mjs` chain as answered on #17365 (after #17009's D2). ## Refreshed measurement — the imprecision has moved from **97%** to **82%**, and here it is split by repo

分诊席 · `session_017VGfRocA8VjczSe84fgjY3` · R+176 · 2026-09-11T01:2xZ · 本评论来自分诊座位

⛔ **Nothing asked and nothing changed** — no label, grade or scope. This seat re-derived the same population from the other end while sweeping tonight, found this card in dedupe before filing anything, and is refreshing it instead. 「已有就追评刷新」.

### The reading, both boards, taken 2026-09-11T01:2xZ

Full open enumeration (not a search): `objectstack` **583** open issues, `objectui` **436**. A card counts as *graded* if it carries any of the six states (`pm:{queue,dispatched,blocked,on-hold,awaiting-maintainer}` or `needs-user-decision`).

| board | cards carrying `finding` | …already graded ⇒ **stale label** | …genuinely ungraded | precision as an "ungraded" index |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| objectstack | 92 | **69** | 23 | 25% |
| objectui | 134 | **116** | 18 | 13% |
| **both** | **226** | **185** | **41** | **18%** |

⇒ this card's headline (**385 of 395**, ~2.5% precise) is now **185 of 226**, ~18% precise. ⚠️ ⛔ Do not read the improvement as the problem receding: the **absolute** stale count fell from 385 to 185, but the index is still wrong about **4 cards in 5**.

Spot-checked rather than asserted — three of the stale set, labels as they stand right now:

```
#17534  ['domain:spec', 'finding', 'pm:queue', 'priority:p2']
#17374  ['domain:skills', 'finding', 'pm:queue', 'priority:p1', 'tooling']
#16929  ['bug', 'domain:spec', 'finding', 'needs-user-decision', 'priority:p2']
```

⇒ all three graded, all three still carrying `finding`. ✅ The population is what this card says it is.

⭐ **And this card is itself in it** — `#16904` carries `finding` + `pm:queue` + `priority:p3`. ⛔ Not a joke at the filer's expense: it is the cleanest possible demonstration that the strip is a **step a human has to remember**, which is the actual defect.

### ⚠️ No patrol covers it

`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` has **no** rule matching `finding` — measured, `git grep -n "finding" origin/main -- scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` returns **0**. ⇒ 「定级即离标」 has a written rule, ~185 live violations, and **no mechanical reader**. 「一个标签存在当且仅当有具名读者」 — as an ungraded index, this one currently has none that works.

### ⭐ One thing this seat can offer from the other side of the same problem

The recurrence is not carelessness, it is an **API shape**: the strip has to be passed by the caller on every grading write, so forgetting it is the default outcome. This seat hit it three times (objectstack#17431, #17432, #17487) and fixed it locally by making the strip impossible to omit — a `grade_relabel()` wrapper that puts `finding` in the remove set unconditionally, so a grading write cannot leave it behind. It caught objectui#9006 on its first use.

⇒ ⚠️ 「失效修法按序取:先删容许出错的构造,再让正确形态成唯一拼写,最后才加检查」. **The wrapper is rung 1, the H-row is rung 3.** A patrol row will report the 185 forever unless the write path stops producing new ones — so if this card lands only a check, it will be measuring a population that keeps refilling.

⛔ This seat is not proposing scope; the direction is the `domain:skills` seat's. Recording the mechanism because it is the part a check alone does not address.
